text:
marina: CobaltMed opened a dispute on INV-2026-1102 — weekend emergency scale produced a $7,200 Dedicated overage in europe-west1 on top of their $22,000 commit. They say our provisioner removed the reserved nodepool labels during scale-out and want the overage reversed. Dropping this here to triage.

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2026-1102 generated for CobaltMed — total $29,200 (overage $7,200). Payment due in 30 days.

luke-acct: CS says CobaltMed's SREs observed new nodes coming up without the reserved nodepool label; they saw the third-party provisioner reattach with empty labels and then manual remediation. They're asking for a credit or shared recovery with the vendor.

esteban-eng: Quick allocator audit: found provision events where labels were cleared by the external agent. Example log snippet: `2026-11-07T02:04:12Z PROVISION node=node-93 action=attach labels={}` then `METER -> on-demand`. Metering attributes based on labels at allocation time so reservation didn't match.

esteban-eng: This looks like a vendor-side bug in the provisioner hook. We can produce an attribution CSV (allocation IDs, timestamps, measured SKU) and patch our metering fallback to prefer reservation tokens in the request metadata, but the permanent fix needs a vendor update.

maya-cs: CobaltMed is a strategic account. They asked for a full re-credit if vendor accepts responsibility; otherwise they'd accept a shared-cost resolution. They're pushing for quick turnaround.

nora-legal: Legal note: avoid placing liability on a third party in customer-facing wording. Frame any adjustment as a "one-time reconciliation" and include a release: credit in full settlement, no admission of fault. If we pursue vendor recovery, do that separately with the vendor contract team.

marina: Finance proposal: one-time goodwill credit of 60% of the overage ($4,320) pending signed settlement from CobaltMed, conditioned on vendor incident ID for recovery pursuit. Approve?

ben: Approved provisionally. Finance to prepare credit memo pending signed settlement. CS to collect vendor incident reference. Eng to produce the attribution CSV and start a vendor RCA ticket.

maya-cs: I'll send the settlement template to CobaltMed now and request the vendor incident ID. Will post back with the signed doc.
